planting.note: Set divisions or transplants out in spring once soil is workable; this selection takes a full season to establish before producing its characteristic petal-less cones.

directions: Green Wizard is a striking selection of the western coneflower that forgoes showy ray petals entirely, instead topping each stem with a tall black cone ringed by bright green bracts. Unlike many drought-tough rudbeckias, it prefers consistently moist, average garden soil and sulks through prolonged dry spells. Plant in full sun among other prairie perennials where its odd silhouette and late-summer bloom provide textural contrast, and leave stems standing into winter since the dried cones hold up well both outdoors and in cut arrangements. Deadheading encourages a longer bloom window but is not required for plant health.

planting.note: Set out nursery transplants in spring; this selection was bred to flower reliably in its first year and to persist longer than the typical short-lived species.

directions: Blackjack Gold was bred from the wild brown-eyed Susan to bloom more freely and persist as a true perennial rather than the biennial habit typical of the species. Branching, dark-red stems carry a profusion of small golden daisies with raised black-brown cones from late summer well into fall, creating a billowy cloud of color that pairs well with asters and grasses. Grow in full sun to light shade in average, well-drained soil, where established clumps show good resistance to foliar disease. The abundant seed heads draw goldfinches and other songbirds through winter if left uncut.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost or set out transplants after frost danger passes; this short-lived selection flowers heavily its first year and often behaves as a biennial thereafter.

directions: Chocolate Orange produces large, two-toned daisies with a wide band of deep chocolate-mahogany surrounding each petal tip in bright golden orange, a striking departure from the solid-gold wild type. Plants bloom profusely from midsummer through frost on a compact, well-branched habit suited to containers, borders, and mass bedding. Grow in full sun and moderately fertile, well-drained soil, watering regularly to keep the continuous bloom coming. As a short-lived perennial it is often treated as an annual or biennial, so allow some flowers to set seed if self-sowing for next season is desired.

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, or direct sow once soil has warmed; this strain is grown as an annual or short-lived perennial and flowers reliably from seed in its first year.

directions: Goldilocks is a long-grown seed strain notable for its semi-double to fully double golden-yellow blooms, a fuller flower form than the single daisies of the wild species, each centered on a dark contrasting eye. The sturdy, well-branched plants hold their flowers well above the foliage, making them useful both in borders and as cut flowers. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil; deadheading spent blooms keeps new flowers coming through the season. Though often grown as an annual bedding plant, it can persist as a short-lived perennial in favorable sites.
